correctness.rationale: The graph metric is one on original edges and apex edges, two on every other distinct pair. Unit tensors with coordinate inner product 1/2 have scaled squared norm 8/3 and squared separation (16/3)(1−2^(−k)) at Hamming distance k; equality at k=2 fixes the noncontracting normalization and the unit edges realize the stated expansion. In an arbitrary Hilbert embedding based at the apex, with t=C², Parseval gives R≤t and the one-flip energy gives U≤dt/4. A degree-j Walsh character changes sign on j(d−j) unordered two-flips, giving mean squared separation 8(dU−V)/(d(d−1))≥4. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives V≥U²/t, and dU−U²/t increases on [0,dt/4], proving t≥8(d−1)/(3d) for all d≥2. This suffices for the exact limit. For the finite LP, Gram averaging preserves every affine squared-distance bound and PSD. Translation invariance diagonalizes the Gram matrix on Walsh characters, and permutation invariance groups the nonnegative masses by degree. At Hamming shell k the corresponding character average is the stated Krawtchouk sum. The degree-zero mass can be removed without violating the apex lower bound because 4≤a₂≤4 times the remaining mass. Conversely every feasible mixture is a real PSD Gram matrix with precisely the required distances. There is a compact feasible sublevel using the tensor upper bound, so the LP has a minimum. At d=2, a₂=4w₁ forces w₁≥1 and a₁=2w₁+4w₂≥2; w₁=1,w₂=0 attains t=2. An independent rational LP reproduction found t=2,2,2,20/9 for d=2,3,4,5, with numerical checks through d=12, not a proof of the infinite claim. Ordinary Hamming and Johnson graph theorems do not retain the cone's metric; same-day clique-join and tree records have different families, even where a finite special case or a limiting number coincides. residual_risks: A broad primary-literature lookup did not yield relevant evidence; this is not an absence claim. Work phrased as a capped-cube or one-point metric extension under different terminology could still exist.

value.rationale: A universal hub changes the usual cube's diverging distortion into a bounded diameter-two problem. The exact limiting obstruction is not set by the diameter alone: the one- and two-coordinate shells compete with the common apex radius, and the feature map meets the resulting constant. This supplies a precise benchmark for one-point extensions of product metrics. The orbit-sized LP additionally makes the exact finite invariant accessible without a Gram matrix of exponential order, without claiming a finite closed form.
